S39.02.note: If the workspace sets agiWorkforce.optOut.memory, the switch cannot turn memory on there (message "Memory stays off here"). The code for a chat turn that skips memory was not run.
steps: Press Cmd+Shift+P, type "Code: Open Settings", press Enter.
Click "Instructions & editor" in the left list (it shows as Instructions & editor).
In the Memory card, switch "Use saved memory facts" off.
Press Cmd+Shift+P, run "Code: Add Memory Fact", type a fact, press Enter.
Compare: a dialog says "Memory is off, so saved facts are not sent with any turn." and no fact is saved, as Expected says.
S39.02.where: Code: Open Settings > Instructions & editor > Memory > Use saved memory facts (switch)

S39.04.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account with saved facts
S39.04.note: When signed out, the list shows "Sign in to see your memory" instead of facts.
steps: Press Cmd+Shift+P, type "Code: Memory", press Enter.
Click "List & remove facts".
Compare: every saved fact appears in the list, under its topic heading.
S39.04.where: Command Palette > Code: Memory > List & remove facts

labels.text: Your account memory, shared with every AGI client…

S39.05.needs: a signed-in account with at least two saved facts
S39.05.note: The search also matches the source and date line under each fact.
steps: Open "Code: Memory" > "List & remove facts".
Type a word that appears in one saved fact.
Compare: only matching facts stay in the list. Delete the text to see all facts again.
S39.05.where: Command Palette > Code: Memory > List & remove facts, then the search box at the top of the list

S39.06.needs: a signed-in account with facts in at least two topics
S39.06.note: A fact with no topic is listed under "Facts".
steps: Open "Code: Memory" > "List & remove facts".
Look for topic headings with a count, such as "Preferences", "Decisions", "Facts", "Context", "Summaries" or "Skills".
Compare: each fact sits under the topic it was saved with. Topics with no facts do not appear.
S39.06.where: Command Palette > Code: Memory > List & remove facts (topic headings in the list)

labels.text: Saved to your account, on every client.

S39.10.note: The fact is sent with chat turns only while Memory is on.
steps: Press Cmd+Shift+P, type "Code: Add Memory Fact", press Enter.
Type "I prefer Python over JavaScript for data work." and press Enter.
Read the message "Saved to your account, on every client."
Open "Code: Memory" > "List & remove facts" and find the new fact.
Compare with Expected: ask a chat question that the fact would answer.
S39.10.where: Command Palette > Code: Add Memory Fact (also Code: Memory > Add a memory fact)

labels.text: Saved to your account, on every client.

S39.11.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account and a file open in the editor
S39.11.note: No "remember" action inside the chat itself was found; the chat /memory command only opens the Memory list.
steps: Open any file and select a sentence.
Right-click the selection and click "Code: Remember This".
Compare: the "Add Memory Fact" box opens with the selected text filled in. Press Enter.
Read the message "Saved to your account, on every client."
S39.11.where: Editor: select text, right-click it, choose "Code: Remember This"

S39.12.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account with Memory on
S39.12.note: The save is done by the server and the AGI CLI after a turn. The VS Code code has no control for it, and which turns qualify, and whether CLI on-device memory reaches this list, were not confirmed.
steps: Have a normal chat that states a lasting preference, such as "I usually write tests in pytest."
Wait for the reply to finish.
Open "Code: Memory" > "List & remove facts".
Compare: a new fact from that chat is listed, as Expected says.
S39.12.where: Effect seen in "Code: Memory" > "List & remove facts" after ordinary AGI Code chats

labels.text: Updated in your account, on every client.

S39.13.needs: a signed-in account with at least one saved fact
steps: Open "Code: Memory" > "List & remove facts".
Hover a fact and click the pencil button "Edit this fact".
Change the text and press Enter.
Read the message "Updated in your account, on every client."
Compare: reopen the list and check the new text is shown; then ask a chat question the fact should change.
S39.13.where: Command Palette > Code: Memory > List & remove facts, then the edit button on a fact row

labels.text: Deleted from your account, on every client.

S39.14.needs: a signed-in account with at least one saved fact
steps: Open "Code: Memory" > "List & remove facts".
Hover a fact and click the trash button "Delete this fact".
Read the dialog and click "Delete".
Read the message "Deleted from your account, on every client."
Compare: the fact is gone from the list.
S39.14.where: Command Palette > Code: Memory > List & remove facts, then the trash button on a fact row

labels.text: All memory facts deleted from your account.

S39.15.needs: a signed-in account with saved facts
S39.15.note: The Memory list itself has no separate delete-all button; this is the one-action path found.
steps: Press Cmd+Shift+P, type "Code: Memory", press Enter.
Click "Clear account memory".
Read the dialog ("Delete all N memory facts from your Cloud account?") and click "Forget everything".
Read the message "All memory facts deleted from your account."
Compare: open "List & remove facts" and check no facts remain.
S39.15.where: Command Palette > Code: Memory > Clear account memory

S39.17.needs: a signed-in account with facts from more than one source (a typed fact and a chat-saved fact)
S39.17.note: The code says "Saved from an import" for imports and has no "typed by you" wording.
steps: Open "Code: Memory" > "List & remove facts".
Hover a fact (or read its detail line) to see where it came from.
Compare: facts typed in VS Code show "Saved from VS Code"; facts from a chat show "Saved from the conversation" with its title; facts with no recorded source show "Source not recorded".
S39.17.where: Command Palette > Code: Memory > List & remove facts, then the detail line under a fact

S39.18.needs: a signed-in account with at least one saved fact
S39.18.note: The "Updated:" line appears only when the update time differs from the creation time.
steps: Open "Code: Memory" > "List & remove facts".
Hover a fact and read the "Created:" line.
Edit that fact with the pencil button "Edit this fact" and save.
Reopen the list and hover the same fact.
Compare: an "Updated:" line now appears under "Created:".
S39.18.where: Command Palette > Code: Memory > List & remove facts, then hover a fact

labels.text: Workspace memory, kept apart from your personal memory
Read in your personal chats on every device

S39.26.needs: an AGI Cloud account that belongs to a workspace, with a personal account memory and a workspace memory to compare
S39.26.note: The workspace row appears only when the account is in a workspace; clicking it opens Team settings on the web.
steps: Open "Code: Memory" > "List & remove facts".
Read the first row: "Personal memory" with "Read in your personal chats on every device", or "<workspace name> memory" with "Workspace memory, kept apart from your personal memory".
Hover that row to read the separation text.
Compare: workspace facts appear only in workspace chats, and personal facts only in personal chats.
S39.26.where: Command Palette > Code: Memory > List & remove facts, first row

S39.29.needs: a signed-in AGI Cloud account and a test term
S39.29.note: No credential or password check was found in the extension files read, so automatic refusal of credentials is unverified.
steps: Press Cmd+Shift+P, type "Code: Memory", press Enter.
Click "Never remember…".
Click "Add a term", type a client or project name, press Enter.
Compare: the term appears under "Never remembered".
Run "Code: Add Memory Fact" with a sentence containing that term and compare: it should be refused.
S39.29.where: Command Palette > Code: Memory > Never remember…, then Add a term

S39.30.needs: a signed-in account with saved facts and at least one chat
S39.30.note: No link from deleting a chat to the memory store was found in the chat state code, so the chat-deletion half could not be located; sign-out also clears the local memory cache.
steps: Note the chats you have in the sidebar.
Press Cmd+Shift+P, run "Code: Memory", click "Clear account memory", then "Forget everything".
Compare: the chats are still listed, and "List & remove facts" shows no facts.
S39.30.where: Command Palette > Code: Memory > Clear account memory (memory reset only)

S39.31.needs: a signed-in account with Memory on and a saved fact
S39.31.note: Memory is added to every turn by the same code path; the model is not checked in it.
steps: With Memory on and a fact saved (for example "I prefer Python over JavaScript for data work"), open the "AGI Code" chat and pick a model.
Ask a question the fact answers, such as "What language should you use for my data scripts?"
Switch to a different model in the chat and ask the same question again.
Compare: both replies use the saved fact.
S39.31.where: Effect seen in the "AGI Code" chat, with any model picked

labels.text: Saved to your account, on every client.

S39.32.needs: a second client (web app, CLI or mobile) signed in to the same account
S39.32.note: The other clients' memory screens were not read, so where to look in them is unverified.
steps: In VS Code, run "Code: Add Memory Fact" and save a fact such as "I prefer Python over JavaScript for data work."
Open the web app, the CLI or mobile on the same account and look for that fact.
Compare: the fact appears there and is used in their chats, as Expected says.
Edit or delete the fact in VS Code and check the other client again.
S39.32.where: Effect seen in the AGI Cloud web app, the AGI CLI or mobile, signed in to the same account
